Stated Claim / Post Context:
CNN star Jake Tapper clashes with Trump's UN ambassador as he begs live on air for his network to be let back into press pool

CNN anchor Jake Tapper confronted President Donald Trump's UN Ambassador Mike Waltz  in a Sunday interview.

Actual Article Body:
By VICTORIA CHURCHILL, US POLITICAL REPORTER

Updated:  06:20 AEST, 28 September 2026

CNN anchor Jake Tapper confronted President Donald Trump's UN Ambassador Mike Waltz in a Sunday interview.

At the end of his wide-ranging conversation with Waltz, Tapper urged him to intervene with President Donald Trump over the White House's decision to bar his network from the press pool.

Before ending the chat, Tapper criticized the administration for preventing CNN from fulfilling its pool assignment on behalf of five major television networks.

'I would just ask if you could please convey to President Trump to let CNN back in the pool,' Tapper said.

'It was not OK when President Obama tried to freeze FOX out of the pool back in 2009. And I don't think we want a world where presidents decide who gets to cover them.'

Waltz pushed back, doubling down on Trump's attack on certain news organizations, which he has accused of biased reporting.

'Well, I hear you, Jake, but I think we need fair and objective and well-sourced reporting,' Waltz responded.

The ambassador then went on to claim that he and his family had personally suffered from misleading coverage.

CNN anchor Jake Tapper pushed Trump's UN Ambassador Mike Waltz about the President's media ban in an interview on his show Sunday

CNN White House Reporter Kaitlan Collins has been vocal about the Trump administration's ban of her and her colleagues this month

'We need a free and fair and honest press corps without an agenda that tries to take facts to fit a narrative,' he said.

Waltz then cited coverage of former President Joe Biden by CNN, and rejected suggestions that Trump was targeting outlets simply for publishing unfavorable stories.

The UN ambassador also pointed to continued White House access for the Washington Post and New York Times, which have also published stories that the Trump Administration has considered to be unfavorable.

'So that's a false narrative that it's about negative reporting,' Waltz argued.

Tapper challenged that explanation, citing Trump's own remarks.

'President Trump specifically said that there's something wrong with a country where people are allowed to report things that are purposely negative,' Tapper countered. 'That's his language, not mine.'

Waltz maintained that Trump was referring to overall media bias, criticizing negative narratives and anonymous sourcing.

'So, this needs to be fixed, and President Trump is quite frustrated with this – this media bias across the board.'

Tapper then ended the exchange with a pointed reminder, 'As has every single president that I've ever covered been frustrated with the press.'

In solidarity with the banned outlets, which also included MS NOW and Politico, major broadcasters like Fox News, NBC, CBS and ABC – known as the TV pool responsible for providing presidential coverage on a rotating basis – have refused to cover the President in response.

Trump banned the news outlets earlier this month in a fiery social media post accusing them of peddling 'fake news.'

He was reportedly shown a slate of negative coverage from the outlets by his aide Natalie Harp in the moments before the ban was announced.

Days later, the White House made a stunning U-turn on its media ban on Thursday, allowing reporters back in after initially turning them away before Xi Jinping and Donald Trump's summit late last week.

'CNN was allowed back into the White House on Thursday at noon,' host Kaitlan Collins posted on X after the debacle.

The White House had initially turned away multiple members of the press on Thursday, even after a judge reinstated access to the banned outlets just hours before.

US District Judge Timothy Kelly granted a temporary restraining order early Thursday morning, effectively forcing the Trump administration to restore access to Politico, CNN and MS NOW, which the President banned the Friday before last.
